author: massicomar
title: Frog 1
summary:
There are $N$ stones, numbered $1, 2, \ldots, N$. For each $i$ ($1 \leq i \leq N$), the height of Stone $i$ is $h_i$.

There is a frog who is initially on Stone $1$. He will repeat the following action some number of times to reach Stone $N$:

- If the frog is currently on Stone $i$, jump to Stone $i + 1$ or Stone $i + 2$. Here, a cost of $|h_i - h_j|$ is incurred, where $j$ is the stone to land on.

Find the minimum possible total cost incurred before the frog reaches Stone $N$.

Input

Input is given from Standard Input in the following format:

$N$
$h_1$ $h_2$ $\ldots$ $h_N$

Output

Print the minimum possible total cost incurred.
explanation: The cost to reach stone i only depends on how you reached stone i−1 or i−2, so a 1D table over stones is enough.
traps: Greedily taking the cheaper next jump is not optimal.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[i] = minimum total cost to reach stone i
dp[i][j] = minimum cost to go from stone i to stone j
options.why: N² states (1e10) and you only ever start from stone 1.

options.text: dp[h] = minimum cost to reach a stone of height h
options.why: Heights don't identify stones, and the order of stones matters.

options.text: dp[i] = number of ways to reach stone i
options.why: That counts paths; the problem asks for a minimum cost.

extraLayers.explanation: The only thing the future needs to know is the best cost to stand on stone i.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.why: That's the counting recurrence (Fibonacci), not a minimum cost.

options.text: dp[i] = min over all j < i of dp[j] + |h_i − h_j|
options.why: That allows jumps of any length (that's Frog 2 with K = N); here only +1 and +2 are allowed.
Mixes two different predecessors: the +2 jump doesn't start from stone i−1.

extraLayers.explanation: You arrive at i from i−1 or i−2; take the cheaper of the two.

es.explanation: El costo de llegar a la piedra i solo depende de cómo llegaste a la piedra i−1 o i−2, así que alcanza con una tabla 1D sobre las piedras.
traps: Tomar con greedy el salto siguiente más barato no es óptimo.

dp-state.explanation: Lo único que el futuro necesita saber es el mejor costo para estar parado en la piedra i.

why.b: N² estados (1e10), y siempre arrancas desde la piedra 1.
why.c: Las alturas no identifican a las piedras, y el orden de las piedras importa.
why.d: Eso cuenta caminos; el problema pide un costo mínimo.

dp-transition.explanation: Llegas a i desde i−1 o desde i−2; quédate con el más barato de los dos.

why.b: Esa es la recurrencia de conteo (Fibonacci), no un costo mínimo.
why.c: Eso permite saltos de cualquier largo (es Frog 2 con K = N); acá solo se permiten +1 y +2.
why.d: Mezcla dos predecesores distintos: el salto de +2 no sale de la piedra i−1.
